verdicts.note: Self-identifies as female ('as a female there are more advantages'); study interviews women.
Confirms aeronautical engineering ('doing aeronautical engineering then? Yeah').
'just a normal high school' plus explicit 'No' to all-girls' school = mixed sex.
'it's really interesting... I want to know how it works' = strong attraction to interesting work.
'I had a knack for maths and physics' explicitly drove the choice; strongly agree justified.
Lifelong technical hobbies (Meccano, Lego, model planes); strongly agree justified.
'liked it because it was so broad... electrical to mechanical to systems' = chose for variety.
'very much my dad's influence... took me to model car racing/plane flying from a very early age'.
Disagree rests on absence; quote is about the father, mother never cited. Low confidence appropriate.
Parents explicitly not engineers; dad is a tech teacher/computer technician, not in the industry.
Advisor reacted positively and suggested engineering areas; reactive approval, agree (not 5) fits.
Quote is mainly about teacher praising the university 'as an engineer'; only indirect encouragement to study engineering — downgrade to low.
Uniformly positive reactions throughout; nobody discouraged her. 'no' supported.
'Very pleased. I don't think I would have taken any other course' = strongly agree.
'this year's really good, actually learning how to design an aircraft from scratch' = very satisfied with design.
Reuses the choice-quote about breadth, but evidences positive sentiment on subject variety; satisfied is conservative.
Best thing about course is the cohort 'gelled really well' = very satisfied with friends.
Personal tutor 'a brilliant chap, really interesting' = very satisfied.
'the lecturer was great on it' re thermodynamics support = satisfied with lecturer support.
Generally likes group work ('I do in most situations... I like everybody'); one difficult peer keeps it at satisfied not 5.
Quote is mainly about task-division benefits, but teamwork/cross-checking maps to interpersonal-skill development; agree moderate.
Quote ('men especially will listen to you') is about being heard as a female, NOT about male vs female confidence in class; variable not addressed — reject.
Explicit 'I'm not.' going on placement; doing straight masters.
Wants to finish in a row ('5 years is too long', 'brains in the right gear'), but the 'start earning money' element is absent — keep agree, lower confidence.
Cites RAF management/leadership training as making her 'bold enough... without the gap year'; agree fits.
RAF volunteer/bursary ('wouldn't be allowed to do a gap year') = Armed Forces reason against placement.
Career aim is RAF (navigator/engineer, 16-year bursary) = Armed Forces related.
'I would really enjoy the people management' = managerial; some pull toward technical but stated preference is managerial.
Doing the integrated 4-year masters; mapped to further study = yes per standard treatment.
'4 years masters' = Masters/MSc/MBA.
Factors becoming chartered into her route choice and checks it carries over to RAF = important.
'Very much good promotional prospects' is her first/top company criterion = very important.

Quote ('they've taken me all around the world') describes RAF travel she has enjoyed, not that travel is an important factor in CHOOSING a job; her stated job criteria were promotion/strong company — reject.
Awkward mapping for a non-placement student, but she affirms placement improves job chances ('if just a Bachelor's I'd be a bit worried'); agree justified.
